reason.correction: The earlier zero-retry wording did not distinguish a harness re-executing a measured operation from a provider attempt made inside a single product-native structured-output or embedding operation. Pinned Cognee 1.5.3 fault injection showed three provider completions after malformed JSON while the adapter itself had invoked one native structured-output operation. Treating all five possible mechanisms as the same retry would either hide real provider usage or reject measured product behavior without a fair, arm-neutral rule. This amendment defines the boundary prospectively.

retryTaxonomy.appliesTo: every arm, every root operation, every provider request class, and every future non-scored v1.1 run identically

A.name: harness-measured-operation-reexecution
A.meaning: The adapter or harness invokes persist, retrieve, reset, or verify again after that root operation has failed or completed.

B.name: provider-transport-retry
B.meaning: A provider client or transport resends a request because of a transport, timeout, or provider error.

C.name: native-structured-output-validation-or-repair
C.meaning: Inside one root operation, a product-native structured-output implementation makes another provider request to validate or repair malformed output.

D.name: structured-output-mode-fallback
D.meaning: Inside one root operation, a product-native implementation changes structured-output mode while keeping the same pinned provider, endpoint, and model.

E.name: model-or-provider-fallback
E.meaning: A product-native implementation substitutes a different model, endpoint, provider, or credential route.

evidenceRule.rootOperationTrace: The progress/unit correlation names one root operation; provider attempt and completion ledgers are reconciled against its adapter operation counters.
evidenceRule.faultInjection: An arm that relies on C or D must demonstrate the selected pinned runtime and configuration with a loopback-only adversarial probe before a live run. The probe cannot contact an external provider.
evidenceRule.failureTreatment: An operation that exhausts its native behavior, reaches a provider cap, times out, or produces ledger disagreement is FAILED. Native success is never relabelled as a new harness attempt.

prospectiveEffect.note: Runs 002 and 003 retain the bytes, retry semantics, statuses, and findings they actually recorded. They are not resubmitted, rescored, or used to satisfy this amendment's pre-run evidence requirement.

countDerivation.rule: Unchanged. The amendment changes neither the arm matrix nor the scenario, seed, repetition, phase, reset, or outer-decision derivation.
